summary: David L. Haberman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1970–1974). He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (~1993).

David L. McMahan works in Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, and served as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013) at Franklin & Marshall College.

David L. Snellgrove (1920–2016) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Southampton, Christ's Hospital, and Cambridge under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, H. W. Bailey, Walter Simon, and Giuseppe Tucci, he served at SOAS, University of London (~1950–1982; Professor attested 1988).
David Ludden is a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia (~1978–1979), the University of Pennsylvania (~1979–2007), and New York University (~2007).

David M. DiValerio works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the School for International Training and the University of Virginia (PhD attested 2011) under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, among others, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor (attested 1975, 1998–2001) and Professor of South Asian Studies and Chair of Religious Studies (attested 1989).
David Matsumoto works in the field of Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, serving as Director (attested 2004) and holding an affiliation attested in 2013.

David N. Keightley (1932–2017) was a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley, including Professor (attested 1985) and an appointment attested in 1999.

David N. Lorenzen specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at SOAS and the Australian National University (~1968–1972) under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and others, and was a Professor and Research Scholar at El Colegio de México (~1972–2012).

David Ownby specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and history. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1980–1989) and held posts at Harvard (1991), Southern Methodist University (attested 1994), and the Université de Montréal (~1993, 1994) as Professor of History.

David P. Jackson works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees at the University of Washington (PhD ~1979–1985) under David Seyfort Ruegg and traditional teachers, and served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, having also studied under Geshe Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and held posts as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree (1933–2005) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, and held positions at Harvard (1960–1963), the University of Chicago (1963–1971), and Brown University (Professor from 1971).

David R. Loy specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton College, the University of Hawaii, and the National University of Singapore (PhD until 1984), he taught at NUS (~1978–1984) and Xavier University (~2006–2014).

David Ralph Quinter specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and served as associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey (1917–2005) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, he held fellowships there and at Jesus College, and later taught at the University of Michigan (1968–1975) and Harvard (1975–1982).
David Ruddell (1943–2015) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.
David Schaberg is a Sinologist who studied at Stanford University (~1982–1986) and Harvard University (~1990–1996). He has held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1996).

David Seyfort Ruegg (1931–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Paris and EHESS under Filliozat, Renou, Lalou, and Stein, later holding professorships at Leiden (1966–1972), Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (attested 2010).
